subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Bubble Tea: Taiwan's Sweet Invention
description: A micro-lesson that makes Bubble Tea: Taiwan's Sweet Invention usable.

hook.text: Bubble tea was invented in Taiwan in the 1980s when someone added tapioca pearls to iced milk tea—and created a global craze.

buildup.text: Two Taiwanese tea shops both claim the invention. Chun Shui Tang and Hanlin Tea Room have disputed credit for decades.

discovery.text: The chewy tapioca pearls (called 'boba') transformed tea from a simple drink into an interactive, textural experience.

twist.text: A Taiwanese court ruled in 2019 that bubble tea cannot be patented—it's too simple. No one owns the invention.

climax.text: Bubble tea is now a multi-billion dollar global industry. From Taipei to London, boba shops outnumber many traditional cafés.

punchline.text: Tapioca in tea—simple, addictive, unstoppable. A snack-drink conquered the world.

quiz.question: Where was bubble tea invented?
options: Taiwan in the 1980s when tapioca pearls were added to iced milk tea
